Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

about preposition

concerning, on the subject of

also concerning, on (a subject), regarding, talk about, think about, a story about

classical

Hor. S. 1.1.69–70: dē tē fābula narrātur
Cic. Att. 5.1.3: sermō isque multus dē tē fuit
Traupman 267

dē + abl.

preposition with the ablative

about, concerning

With verbs of speaking, writing, hearing and thinking, and in titles: Dē senectūte.

Other words

  • super + abl. — about, concerning

    preposition with the ablative · also used · classical · Verg. A. 1.750: multa super Priamō rogitāns; Cic. Att. 16.6.1: hāc super rē scrībam ad tē Rhēgiō (Lewis & Short)

    (in this sense chiefly in comedy, poetry and post-Augustan prose; a few times in Cicero’s letters (Lewis & Short))

Examples

  • quid rīdēs? mūtātō nōmine dē tē fābula narrātur

    why are you laughing? change the name, and the story is about youHor. S. 1.1.69–70

  • ut vēnī in Arpīnās, cum ad mē frāter vēnisset, in prīmīs nōbīs sermō isque multus dē tē fuit

    when I reached Arpinum and my brother had come to see me, our first talk, and a long one, was about youCic. Att. 5.1.3

  • habēs ferē dē rēbus rūsticīs

    that is about all on country mattersCic. Q. fr. 3.1.6

  • dīc sōdēs, inquit Fundānius; nam mālō dē meīs pedibus audīre, quam quem ad modum pedēs bētāceōs serī oporteat

    “Tell me, please,” said Fundanius, “for I’d rather hear about my feet than about how beet feet ought to be planted”Varr. RR 1.2.27

  • Nūlla tam bona est fortūna, dē quā nīl possīs querī.

    No luck is so good that you can find nothing in it to complain about.Publil. Sent. N 8

  • multa super Priamō rogitāns, super Hectore multa

    asking many things about Priam, many about HectorVerg. A. 1.750

See also according to.
